title: per-route-size-heuristics-and-adaptive-slab-buffering-for-stream-toolcalls
author: Asha Kapoor
release_notes: Introduce per-route payload heuristics and an adaptive slab buffer layer in the gateway to reduce streaming fragmentation and stabilize function/tool call handshakes. Improves OpenAI-compat fallbacks under load.
description:
Motivation: We observed increased tail latency and fragmented streaming sequences for long toolcall/structured-output sessions under mixed workloads. This surfaced as duplicate handshake attempts for OpenAI-compat clients and intermittent truncation when route-specific payloads exceeded transient buffer windows. The change introduces two complementary mitigations: (1) per-route size heuristics that dynamically clamp effective payload windows based on recent sequence-size histograms and route SLAs, and (2) an adaptive "slab" buffering layer in the streaming proxy that groups ingress fragments into sized slabs for more deterministic writer-side flushes.

Summary of changes: - Gateway: add RouteSizeHeuristic component that tracks per-route percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and exposes a lightweight decision API for the ingress path. - Gateway config: new route config flag `heuristic_window_ms` and `heuristic_max_payload_bytes` with sane defaults and ability to override per-route. - Streaming proxy: introduce slab buffer abstraction (slab size is adaptive based on moving average of fragment sizes and latency budget) and explicit slab-ack protocol to reduce partial fragment flushes. - OpenAI-compat shim: update tool/function call handshake to tolerate slab-ack delays and fall back to a legacy byte-stream when repeated handshakes fail. Adds exponential backoff and single-retry suppression to avoid thundering retries. - Observability: add metrics for slab_fill_rate, slab_ack_latency, route_size_percentiles, and compatibility_fallbacks; dashboards and alerts updated. - Tests: new unit tests for RouteSizeHeuristic, integration tests simulating mixed small/large payload mixes, and an end-to-end scenario validating OpenAI-compat handshake under load.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added for heuristic logic and slab buffering [x] Integration tests for streaming proxy under stress [x] Updated docs for route config flags and compat behavior [x] Performance bench runs (internal) demonstrating 18-32% reduction in streaming tail fragmentation for tested workloads [x] Changelog/release notes drafted

Commits (high level): - feat(gateway): route size heuristic + config flags - feat(stream-proxy): adaptive slab buffer + slab-ack protocol - chore(metrics): add slab and heuristic metrics - fix(compat): handshake backoff + legacy fallback - test: add e2e toolcall stress test and unit coverage

Files changed (high level): - gateway/src/routing/route_size_heuristic.go (new) - gateway/config/route_schema.proto (schema bump) - stream-proxy/src/slab_buffer.rs (new) - stream-proxy/src/ack_protocol.rs (new) - compat/openai_shim/handshake.go (tolerate slab ACKs/backoff) - observability/dashboards/slab_buffer.json (dashboard) - tests/e2e/handshake_stress.test (integration fixture) and small build/test harness adjustments

Testing and CI: Initial CI run failed on a flaky integration that surfaced a race in the slab-ack timeout unit. The race was fixed in the second commit by tightening the cancelation ordering and adding a deterministic test hook. CI summary: initial run (fail on streaming-integration) -> fix commit -> full CI pass (unit/integration/e2e). Load tests run in benchmark-lab showed consistent decreases in fragment counts per session and a 25% lower incidence of handshake fallbacks at 95th percentile for our mixed small/large workload profile.

Review conversation (selected highlights): - Sofia Chen (reviewer): "RouteSizeHeuristic looks reasonable but we should ensure the memory footprint is bounded for high-cardinality routes." — Author reply: "Added a ring-sampled histogram with TTL per route and a hard cap on tracked routes; noted in comments and docs." - Marco Alvarez: "slab-ack protocol semantics need clear invariants around reordering and retransmit." — Author: "Added explicit sequence numbers to slab ACKs and a small retransmit window; included tests that simulate out-of-order ACKs." - Priya Subramanian: "Can we avoid changing existing route configs unless opted in?" — Author: "Defaults are zero-config: heuristic is opt-in per-route; when disabled the gateway behaves as before. Updated docs to call out opt-in migration path." - Follow-up from SRE: "Alert for compatibility_fallbacks spike should be moderate severity and tied to slab_ack_latency" — Action: added alert with 15-minute burn rate and notify SRE on escalation.

Backward compatibility and rollout: - Safe by default: heuristics are opt-in per-route (flag in route config). - Canary rollout plan: enable for a small set of internal routes behind feature flags, monitor slab_ack_latency and compatibility_fallbacks metrics, then widen. - Fallback: On repeated handshake failure, gateway transparently downgrades to legacy byte-stream fallback for that session and emits compatibility_fallbacks metric.

Performance notes: Benchmarks run against the benchmark-lab suite with mixed session profiles (chat-like short messages plus episodic toolcalls of 1-2MB total). Results: median latency change is +3% (due to slight extra buffering), p95/p99 streaming fragmentation and handshake failure rates decreased by 18-32% depending on workload, and overall consumed CPU per proxy decreased by ~5% because there are fewer small writes and retransmits.

Security/ops notes: - No new credentials or auth surface added. - RouteSizeHeuristic does not persist user payloads; only size histograms are recorded. - Observability exposes only aggregated percentiles. - Added a migration note for customers using strict per-route size enforcement: a small window exists during canary where heuristics might clamp transient large payloads; docs recommend increasing heuristic_max_payload_bytes if permitted.

Merge outcome: approved by reviewers after two rounds of iteration. CI green on final run. Merged via squash with a single commit containing the aggregated changes and test fixes.

Follow-ups and TODOs: - ENG-7198: expose an admin API to peek per-route heuristic stats for debugging (drafted) - ENG-7239: experiment with predictive slab sizing using model of recent session shapes - Docs PR to redwood-docs scheduled to land next week with config examples and rollout guidance

If you want to test locally: see tests/e2e/handshake_stress.test and run `./dev/bench --scenario=handshake_stress --duration=2m` against a local gateway+proxy compose. For immediate troubleshooting, the route metric `gateway.route_size_percentiles` and `proxy.slab_ack_latency` are the primary signals.
